decisions.reason: The instruction changes the sources and terms used for product messaging, but does not replace the current reference-led creative concept direction.
The keyword revision does not change the independent sourcing or testimonial-style presentation of the testimonial material.
The same message's Hindi-only clause is already fully represented by the candidate's INTRODUCE Event; the reference-keyword change requires no additional localization update.
Rejecting generic keyword wording does not change the existing requirement that the opening hook be direct and suitable for the Indian market.
The source changes product-message terminology but leaves the independently required viral creative style unchanged.
The reference-derived keyword policy does not change the specified audience age range or market context.
The source does not mention or alter the call-to-action requirement.
The messaging revision does not resolve or otherwise affect the production-method conflict concerning live-action and AI-generated visuals.
The source contains no change to lip-sync accuracy or facial-expression requirements.
Changing the required script terminology does not alter responsibility for supplying the script, visuals, or voiceover.
The CPL concern motivates the keyword revision but does not change the existing CPL target or conversion-performance objective.
The messaging decision does not alter the pilot quantity, duration, formats, or follow-on order condition.
